verdicts.reason: The ownership predicate now exists in the statement itself: the same request that returned another owner's invoice before the patch returns an empty result after it, and the SQL log shows the exclusion comes from `AND owner_id = $2` bound to the subject, not from an error. Residual named rather than hidden: the predicate is only as strong as `req.user.id`, and with F-001 unpatched a forged unsigned token resolving to `{id:1}` makes the patched route hand over the victim's invoice again - the patch does what F-002 asked, the exposure closes only when F-001 closes too.
verdicts.checked: Applied to a copy with `git apply -p1`; target/ untouched. In-process harness (stub express Router dispatching handlers directly, lib/db.js swapped in the require cache for a fake backed by the real sqlite3 CLI, $n values bound as literals so an interpolated clause executes as written, node-fetch stub that throws on any network use). VER-08 all three runs: (a) unpatched copy, user 2 GET /invoices/1 -> 200 with the full victim row; (b) benign, patched copy, owner user 1 GET /invoices/1 -> 200 with their row, and the reach evidence is the emitted statement `SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2` with params ["1",1], which only the patched line can produce; (c) patched copy, user 2 GET /invoices/1 -> 200 [] with params ["1",2], no exception, no 500. VER-03 axes: encoding of :id (`01`, trailing space, `%31`, `1' OR '1'='1`, `1 OR owner_id=1`, `1;--`, `1/**/`, NUL) - all blocked, the id is bound not interpolated; verb/route (PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, POST on /invoices/1 -> no route; /receipts/:id, /invoices, /payments all already carry owner_id, so the BOLA class has no other open call site in scope); identity (other tenant, other tenant claiming role admin, missing id, null id - none reads the row; forged-token chain through lib/auth.js currentUser() does, which is F-001). Read the whole route file and the four db.query call sites for other places sharing the broken property (REM-01).
verdicts.not_checked: Timing/race axis - a single read query with no state change, nothing to race. The `if (!invoice) return 404` line added by the patch is dead code: `[]` from the stand-in and a node-postgres Result object are both truthy, so a foreign or missing invoice answers 200 with an empty body instead of 404; harmless for the finding (nothing is disclosed) but it is not the behaviour the patch claims. Behaviour change not covered by the finding: an unauthenticated request (no req.user) now throws TypeError inside the async handler where the unpatched route answered 200 - in express 4 that is an unhandled rejection, not a 401; it matches the three sibling handlers' existing convention. No project test suite exists in this tree (package.json declares it non-installable), so REM-04's before/after suite comparison could not be run. No unskippable scoping layer was introduced, so a future handler can omit the predicate again. The real database and driver were not used: node-postgres text-vs-integer comparison semantics for :id were not exercised. F-001 and F-004 have no patch in this set and were not verified.

verdicts.reason: The patch validates the shape of the identifier and adds nothing about who owns the row, so the original case reproduces verbatim: user 2 requests /invoices/1 with a perfectly numeric id and receives the victim's full invoice row. The check reached the code - the same handler returns 400 on a non-numeric id - and what it established is that the control is on the wrong property (REM-01's symptom-versus-root-cause row: the id was already a bound `$1`, so there was never an injection to filter here).
verdicts.checked: Same harness and same isolated copy. VER-08 all three runs: (a) unpatched copy, user 2 GET /invoices/1 -> 200 with the victim row; (b) benign, patched copy, owner user 1 GET /invoices/1 -> 200 with their row, unchanged, and the reach evidence is GET /invoices/abc -> 400 {"error":"invalid id"}, a response only the patched line can emit; (c) patched copy, user 2 GET /invoices/1 -> 200 with the victim row, statement still `SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1`, no owner predicate. Enumeration axis: ids 1..4 as user 2 returned every row in the table including both of the victim's. Read the diff against the finding's recommendation (`AND owner_id = $2`), which the patch does not implement.
verdicts.not_checked: Variant axes beyond the identifier were not pursued, because the original case reproduces at the first attempt and there is nothing left to bypass. Whether invoice identifiers are integers in production is not in scope (no schema, no migration): if they are UUIDs or prefixed strings, the `^[0-9]+$` test also breaks the benign path, which run (b) here cannot see because the fixture ids are numeric. The interaction of PX-02 with PX-01 (both touch the same handler; the diffs do not conflict textually) was not exercised as a combined patch.

verdicts.reason: The XSS sink is closed - no variant tried produced markup a browser would parse - but check (b) of VER-08 failed and not for a harness reason: 5 of 5 realistic customer notes come out silently mutilated, since `[^a-zA-Z0-9 ]` deletes every period, comma, colon, hyphen, slash, `%`, `@`, `#`, `$`, parenthesis and every accented or non-ASCII character. `Ref: INV-2026/08 - paid in full, balance $0.00` renders as `Ref INV202608  paid in full balance 000` inside a billing document. The finding's own recommended fix, `escapeHtml(note)`, preserves all five strings unchanged, which rules out VER-08's exculpation that the input was never legitimate: the data loss is a property of this patch, not of fixing the bug. Open part, named: functional preservation - the patch should not ship as written.
verdicts.checked:
Applied to a copy; the composer is a module export with no caller in the tree, so (b) was answered at module level (the level is stated per VER-08's clause on paths with no direct request-level benign input). VER-08 all three runs: (a) unpatched copy, `invoiceNote('')` -> `
`, live markup; (b) benign, patched copy, five ordinary notes -> all five altered, diffed against what escape-html@1.0.3's algorithm returns for the same inputs; (c) patched copy, same payload -> `
img srcx onerroralertdocumentdomain
`, inert, and the stripping is the control doing it. VER-03 encoding axis: uppercase tag, HTML entity, double-encoded entity, literal `\u003c` text, fullwidth `＜`, space-in-tag, surrogate pair plus tag, attribute-breakout quotes, `${...}` template syntax, an object with a malicious toString, an array of payloads, null, undefined, number - every one inert, and no bypass found (the class is an allowlist of characters, so encoding tricks have nothing to reach). Confirmed the sibling composers customerName and footer are untouched by the diff and still neutralize their input. VER-01 refutation attempt on the finding itself: grepped the copy for a caller of lib/render.js - none exists, so reachability stays inferred and the finding stays `probable`.
verdicts.not_checked: Reachability of the sink with attacker-controlled text - no caller of invoiceNote exists in scope, so the note travelling from a request into the composer was not observed (this is the finding's own declared inference, unchanged by the patch). The rendered page, its response headers and any CSP are outside the scope, so the browser-side outcome was not observed - the claim of inertness is about the emitted string. Whether notes are meant to carry formatting (in which case a sanitizer, not escaping, is the right control) could not be determined. No project test suite exists to run before and after.

verdicts.reason: Stripping `;` removes a character the exploit never needed. After the patch, `req.query.order` is still concatenated into the ORDER BY clause untouched, and the one-bit oracle from the finding's own evidence works identically before and after: `(CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM invoices WHERE owner_id=1 AND total_cents>100000)>0 THEN total_cents ELSE -total_cents END)` returns the attacker's rows as [3,4] when the condition over the victim's data is true and [4,3] when it is false, executed by a real SQL engine. This is REM-01's cosmetic patch verbatim - filter a metacharacter instead of stopping the identifier from being interpolated.
verdicts.checked: Applied to a copy; the emitted statement was executed by sqlite3, so the ordering is a real result and not a reading of the string. VER-08 all three runs: (a) unpatched copy, the oracle flips row order between the true and false conditions, proving expression-level exfiltration of another owner's data; (b) benign, patched copy, no order parameter, `order=created_at` and `order=total_cents` all return the list normally, and the reach evidence is `order=created_at;` emerging as `ORDER BY created_at` - only the patched line strips that semicolon; (c) patched copy, the same semicolon-free oracle -> same flip, same exfiltration, 200 each time. VER-03 axes: `created_at DESC`, a scalar subquery over the victim's note column, a character-by-character `substr()` oracle, an array-valued `order` parameter (`String()` joins with a comma and both terms reach the clause), a URL-encoded semicolon, and a stacked `; SELECT 1` - the first four all interpolate and execute; the last two only produce a parse error, which is the sole thing the strip achieves. Control comparison: /payments with the same payload resolves through the SORTABLE map and emits `ORDER BY created_at`, the literal the finding points at as the correct pattern.
verdicts.not_checked: The engine used is sqlite3, not the node-postgres/PostgreSQL pair the `$1` placeholders imply, so dialect-specific ceilings were not measured - stacked statements, `pg_sleep` timing, error-text disclosure and what the database role can read outside the invoices table. The direction token (`asc`/`desc`) is not separately validated by the patch and was not probed for a second injection point beyond the array case. `req.query.order` as a nested object (`?order[a]=b`, which express parses into an object and `String()` renders as `[object Object]`) was not exercised. No project test suite exists to run before and after.

verdicts.reason: filter="data" is the class-level control and it holds: through the shipped `packer unpack` entry point every payload shape F-001 names (../.., traversal not at the front, absolute member name, symlink and hardlink escapes, setuid bit) is refused or neutralised on Python 3.12.10 while a benign archive still extracts intact. It is not `verified` because the target pins no interpreter and F-001's own limits field names that gap: on this host's /usr/bin/python3 (3.9.6, older than the filter= backport of 3.9.17) the patched line raises `TypeError: extractall() got an unexpected keyword argument 'filter'` for every archive, so on that environment run (b) fails and run (c) fails through an unrelated error instead of through the control - functional preservation is the named open part.
verdicts.checked: Applied to a copy of target/ with patch -p1 (target/ untouched). VER-08 (a) baseline on unpatched code, python3.12.10: `packer.py unpack` wrote ../CLI-ESCAPED into the parent of the cwd (rc=0), and the function-level harness also escaped with an absolute member name and with a symlink member written through - the finding reproduces for the reason it claims. (b) benign, same client: `packer.py unpack benign.tar` wrote hello.txt into the cwd (rc=0) and the 2-member archive extracted with contents intact - evidence the patched line ran and allowed. (c) attack, patched: rc=1 with tarfile.OutsideDestinationError, AbsoluteLinkError and LinkOutsideDestinationError, i.e. the filter's own signals read from the message; the absolute name was rewritten inside the destination and the 0o4755 member landed as 0o755 (setuid stripped) instead of 0o4755 in the baseline. VER-03 axes: payload/encoding - 7 shapes tried (../../, a/../../, absolute, absolute-target symlink, relative-target symlink, hardlink, setuid); route - main() at packer.py:91-92 has one dispatch and it is unpack, and unpack_safely is untouched and already filtered; identity and timing - not applicable to a file-to-process boundary with one local principal, stated rather than assumed. Environment axis: (a) and (b) re-run under /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6, where baseline still escapes and the patched code TypeErrors on benign and malicious archives alike. py_compile on the patched file returns 0.
verdicts.not_checked: No interpreter between 3.9.17 and 3.11.4 exists on this host, so the exact backport boundary was reasoned from the two versions present (3.12.10 and 3.9.6) rather than measured across the range, and nothing establishes which interpreter a real deployment would use. The hardlink payload aborted with KeyError before the write in both baseline and patched runs, so that member type decided nothing on the baseline side. Decompression bombs (excluded by the finding too), Windows path separators and non-POSIX filesystems were not tried. The target ships no test suite, so REM-04's before/after suite run was answered only with py_compile plus the CLI smoke runs. F-001's recommendation to remove the duplicate unfiltered function and to stop defaulting the destination to the cwd is untouched by this patch and was not verified.

verdicts.reason: The check reached the code and established that the patch does not work: it tests only whether a member name starts with "..", so three payload shapes F-001 names in its own evidence sentence still land outside the destination after the patch - an absolute member name, a symlink member with a later regular member written through it, and a traversal that is not at the front of the name. It also rejects a benign member called ..config, so it costs functionality without covering the class.
verdicts.checked: Applied to a copy of target/ with patch -p1. VER-08 (a) baseline: unpatched `packer.py unpack` escaped with ../CLI-ESCAPED, with an absolute name and with a symlink member. (b) benign: after the patch the 2-member archive still extracts (hello.txt, sub/nested.txt) and the CLI run wrote hello.txt into the cwd, rc=0 - the path still works for ordinary archives. (c) attack: only the literal ../../ payload is stopped, with ValueError: refusing traversal; run through the shipped entry point after the patch, `unpack abs.tar` wrote CLI-ABS and `unpack sym.tar` wrote CLI-SYM into a directory outside the destination, both rc=0, and the function-level harness additionally escaped with a/../../ESCAPE-dotslash. VER-03 axes: payload/encoding - the same 7 shapes as PC-01; route - main()'s single dispatch is the path used for the CLI evidence; identity and timing not applicable. The false rejection of ..config was observed in the same run (ValueError on a benign name).
verdicts.not_checked: The hardlink member aborted with KeyError before the write in both baseline and patched runs, so hardlink escape was not decided here. Windows-style ..\ names, unicode-normalised names and path components hidden behind a PAX header were not tried - unnecessary for the verdict, since the class was already shown open with three named shapes. Interpreter axis not repeated: the bypass is in the patch's own comparison and does not depend on the tarfile version. No second patch was combined with this one.

verdicts.reason: The check reached the patched line and established that the property F-004 is about survives it: `safe = path.lstrip("-").replace("-", "")` deletes every dash anywhere in the name, so sign("release-1.0.tar") made gpg act on release1.0.tar - a different, neighbouring file, whose content in the run was the planted one - which is the finding's own impact, a name the program did not choose deciding what gets signed. The `--` terminator the finding asks for, and which verify() already uses six lines below at packer.py:51, is still absent; the leading-dash option payload is stopped only by a mangling that simultaneously breaks every legitimate dashed release name.
verdicts.checked: Applied to a copy of target/ with patch -p1. gpg is not installed on this host, so the child was a stub placed first on PATH that records the exact argv and parses it with getopt.gnu_getopt over gpg's documented long options; nothing was signed and no key material was touched. VER-08 (a) baseline: sign("--output=<sandbox>/pwned.out") and sign("--homedir=<sandbox>/evil-gnupg") produce argv where the value parses as an option ([['--output', ...]]) with files=[] - the finding reproduces for the reason it claims. (b) benign: sign("release-1.0.tar") on the patched copy delivered files=['release1.0.tar'], exist=True, content b'attacker-planted content\n' - the patched line was reached and the legitimate call was silently redirected onto a file the caller never named. (c) attack: the option payload arrives as a positional, so that specific lever is closed. VER-03 axes: identity/second argument - key_id="--output=..." is consumed as the value of --local-user in both baseline and patched runs, so that axis yields no bypass and is recorded as tried and negative; encoding - U+2212 minus is not an option in either build, an all-dash name collapses to the empty string; route - sign() is the only vector patched and verify() is untouched.
verdicts.not_checked: Real gpg was never invoked: option-versus-file parsing is simulated with getopt.gnu_getopt against gpg's documented long-option interface, not measured against the binary, and the stub raised GetoptError on the baseline all-dash case, which is the stub's limitation and not gpg's. No --output write, no --homedir keyring and no signature were attempted. sign() still has no caller in the target, so F-004's own reachability inference (FP-02 and FP-04 answered UNKNOWN) is unchanged by this run - what was measured is the argument vector, not who supplies the name. The collision the mangling creates between distinct names (a-b.tar and ab.tar both become ab.tar) was demonstrated once, not enumerated.

verdicts.reason: The reported mechanism is closed and the check reached the code: after the patch the token file is 0600 at rest, not group- or world-readable, and the ordinary run still returns a path whose content reads back. Two named parts stay open and both were measured: the file is created 0644 and the complete token is written before the chmod, so a local account that opens it in that window keeps a descriptor the later chmod cannot revoke - F-003 no longer holds as a file that simply sits there readable, but it holds as a race; and CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True) still accepts a foreign shared directory, so a token symlink planted in it still receives the cleartext token and the chmod follows the link, which is F-003's own 'they can replace the token or harvest every future one'.
verdicts.checked: Applied to a copy of target/ with patch -p1. CACHE was rebound to a sandbox directory so the module's logic ran unchanged but nothing was created at the real shared /tmp/packer-cache; the value written was the literal SECRET-TOKEN, no real credential. Process umask measured at 0o22. VER-08 (a) baseline: file mode 0o644, group/world readable True, content SECRET-TOKEN - the finding reproduces for the reason it claims. (b) benign: patched write_token("SECRET-TOKEN") returned the path, the owner read the value back, mode at rest 0o600, and the instrumented os.chmod inside the module namespace fired - evidence the patched line itself ran and allowed the legitimate write. (c) attack, the reported case: the at-rest read by another account is closed by the 0600 mode. The same instrumentation recorded the state at the instant before the narrowing: mode 0o644 with content 'SECRET-TOKEN' already on disk. Second run with the cache directory pre-created 0777 and token planted as a symlink: under both baseline and patch the cleartext token landed in the attacker-side path, and under the patch the chmod applied 0600 to that attacker-owned file, which its owner can widen again.
verdicts.not_checked: This host has one account available to the run, so the cross-user read inside the 0644 window and the foreign-owned cache directory (where the chmod would instead fail with EPERM and crash the call) were demonstrated by construction - modes, ordering and symlink following - and not with a real second uid; no race win rate was measured. Behaviour under a hardened umask was not exercised beyond the measured 0o22. The token remains cleartext on disk in a shared location, and F-003's recommendation to use write_token_privately's construction, delete the /tmp variant or hand the secret to a keystore is untouched and unverified. F-002 (stage(), packer.py:27-32) and F-005 (publish(), packer.py:54-56) received no patch in this set and were not verified at all.
